title: Travel Protection Plans: Rating Manual Footnote on the Days of Cover Bought
content:
The days of cover bought, against which a re-rated difference on a Travel Protection Plans certificate is apportioned, are read from the length of the journey insured, the plan's longest single journey and the standing of the certificate. The journey insured runs from its first day to its last day, both days counted.

Where the journey insured runs longer than the plan's longest single journey, the days of cover bought are the plan's longest single journey.

Where the journey insured runs for the plan's longest single journey or less and the certificate stands expired or cancelled, the days of cover bought are counted from the day the certificate was issued to the last day of the journey insured, both days counted.

Where neither holds, the days of cover bought are counted from the first day of the journey insured to its last day, both days counted.

## The plan's longest single journey

| Plan | Longest single journey, days |
| --- | --- |
| Trip Basics Essential | 30 |
| Trip Basics Standard | 45 |
| TripGuard Plus | 60 |
| TripGuard Premier | 90 |
| Cancel For Any Reason Elite | 90 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Traveller | 30 |
| Annual Multi-Trip Executive | 60 |

## The three measures

The first case is reached on length alone: a journey longer than the plan's longest single journey gives days of cover bought equal to that maximum, whatever the certificate's standing.

The second case requires both that the journey is within the plan's maximum — at the maximum exactly, or less — and that the certificate stands expired or cancelled. Its count begins at the day of issue rather than at the first day of the journey, so it is the longer measure where cover was bought well ahead.

The third case is reached where the journey is within the plan's maximum and the certificate stands in neither of those two states.

Hypothetically, on a plan whose longest single journey is 60 days: a journey of 64 days gives 60 days of cover bought. A journey of 30 days on a certificate standing as expired, issued 12 days before the journey began, gives a count from the issue day to the last day of the journey, both counted, which is 42 days. The same journey on a certificate standing in force gives 30 days.
